title: Chapter 2: A Curious Daily Mission
html:
The app with the Haunted House icon resembled a typical management game, except that instead of running a hotel, aquarium, or pet store, the player managed a Haunted House.

Chen Ge stared at the screen with a single question on his mind. Why would the phone my parents left behind have such a strange app on it?

He studied the app’s interface. Every detail matched the real condition of his Haunted House, from its daily visitor count to its available scenarios. It gave Chen Ge the uncanny feeling that the Haunted House in the game and the one he managed in real life were one and the same.

Both were struggling and on the verge of closing; the similarities were impossible to ignore.

“Could this game be based on my Haunted House? If things change in the game, does that mean they’ll change in real life too?” Chen Ge muttered.

Chen Ge kept reading. The app savaged one of the Haunted House’s current scenarios, Night of the Living Dead. Even Minghun, which had once made the newspapers, earned only a 0.5-star rating.

“If Minghun only gets 0.5 stars, I shudder to imagine how terrifying those locked scenarios are.” He tried tapping one of them, but a message appeared telling him he first had to complete a certain number of Daily Missions.

“So the Daily Missions are the key. Completing them will unlock new haunted scenarios, and more scenarios will attract more visitors. That, in turn, will let me expand the Haunted House.” As an avid mobile gamer, Chen Ge quickly grasped the rules: how well he completed the Daily Missions would determine the Haunted House’s development.

When he tapped Daily Missions, three options appeared:

Easy Mission: A good Haunted House depends on three core elements—story, scenario, and atmosphere. A Haunted House without a story has no soul. Complete the background stories for the two scenarios Night of the Living Dead and Minghun.

Normal Mission: Fix all the mannequins inside the Haunted House before midnight.

Nightmare Mission: I know you’re still not wholly convinced about the existence of ghosts in the world; in that case, how about a little game? The truth will be revealed when you open your eyes.

Daily Missions refresh every day at midnight. The user can accept only one mission each day, and the reward corresponds to the mission’s difficulty.

(Warning! The more difficult the mission, the greater the danger. Choose carefully!)

After reading the mission details, Chen Ge inhaled sharply. “The missions in the game have to be completed in real life? Isn’t that proof that this game can affect reality?!”

To test his theory, he decided to accept a mission. Since rewards scaled with difficulty and he could choose only one mission per day, the most difficult option promised the greatest reward. Even so, the warning at the end made him hesitate.

“This is a tough choice. The Nightmare Mission is so vague; it practically screams trap. Why don’t I start with the Normal Mission? Fixing all the props will be difficult, but not impossible.”

Chen Ge was a man of action. Once he had made his decision, he got to work. He grabbed his toolbox and an unopened bucket of fake blood, then began inspecting every mannequin in the Haunted House.

Night had fallen. To save electricity, Chen Ge did not even turn on the corridor lights. With a flashlight tucked under one arm, he wound his way through the sprawling Haunted House, repairing every mannequin that needed attention.

If anyone had seen him working like that, they probably would have been frightened enough to call the police.

“I really didn’t expect this many mannequins to need maintenance. I shouldn’t have slacked off before!”

At 11:45 p.m., Chen Ge received the mission-completion alert on his phone. “You have completed the Normal Mission. Attention to detail is essential to creating the perfect atmosphere of fear. Congratulations! You have received the mission reward—Background Music: Black Friday.”

“Wait, wasn’t Black Friday banned in some countries? According to the rumors, it had a deeply disturbing effect on its listeners, and the original score was lost long ago.” Chen Ge found an image of a CD in his item storage. “What kind of mission reward is this? Don’t tell me this whole thing is some kind of prank.”

He tapped the CD image, and an unfamiliar melody began to play. The music spoke of darkness, melancholy, and loneliness. Chen Ge felt the world around him fall away, as though he had suddenly found himself in a corridor with no end.

When the song ended, Chen Ge’s back was drenched in cold sweat. He was thankful he had not put it on repeat; otherwise, he doubted he could have broken free of its influence on his own.

“F*ck, it’s real! This must be the original track!” Completing the mission had truly given him a reward he could use in real life. That gave Chen Ge a ray of hope. He stopped the music and carefully saved the file. Once everything was in order, he returned to the break room to rest.

Even though he was exhausted, Chen Ge did not feel sleepy once he lay down. After everything he had experienced that day, he needed time to process it all.

Before he knew it, midnight had passed, and Chen Ge was still staring blankly at the ceiling.

“I can’t sleep at all!” Bored out of his mind, he pulled out the black phone. “It’s past midnight, so there should be a new set of Daily Missions, right?”

He opened the app, and as he expected, there were some changes on the Daily Missions screen.

Easy Mission: If you want to give visitors a frightening experience, you must first pay attention to the rhythm and pacing of their journey through the Haunted House. Triggering a scare too early may dull its effect, so I suggest installing sound detectors or surveillance cameras to track your visitors’ progress.

Normal Mission: One hand cannot clap. A good Haunted House needs a good team to run it. Recruit more talent to aid you on your journey.

Nightmare Mission: I know you’re still not wholly convinced about the existence of ghosts in the world; in that case, how about a little game? The truth will be revealed when you open your eyes.

Daily Missions refresh every day at midnight. The user can accept only one mission each day, and the reward corresponds to the mission’s difficulty.

(Warning! The more difficult the mission, the greater the danger. Choose carefully!)

The three new Daily Missions threw a wrench into Chen Ge’s plans.

The Easy Mission required him to install new surveillance equipment in the Haunted House. Money could solve that problem, but unfortunately, money was exactly what Chen Ge lacked.

The Normal Mission was no easier. Two veteran employees who had stuck with him through thick and thin had just resigned. Even if he posted a recruitment notice immediately, training a new employee would take days. By the time that person was ready to work, the Haunted House might already have closed.

With both the Easy and Normal Missions out of reach, Chen Ge turned his attention to the final Daily Mission.

“The harder the mission, the better the reward. Should I give this Nightmare Mission a try?”
